final_answer.key_evidence_summary: Entry service frontend emits 503s on /product/{id} and /cart while every object-layer surface is healthy: all 11 pods 2/2 Running with 0 restarts, all endpoints bound, all deployments 1/1, 4 nodes Ready/untouched, and live TCP probes to all 8 downstream ports succeed. The only anomalous trail sits in cartservice logs (713/2657 log lines), which show AddItemAsync called with userId=<10-char product id> and productId=<session UUID> -- exactly the swap of frontend's own request fields (product=OLJCESPC7Z, session=deb5f24d-1373-4ee9-af47-3e7523a241c7), while its GetCartAsync calls carry correct session UUIDs. The code surface proves the call site: frontend handlers.go addToCartHandler contains the injected line `userID, productID = productID, userID` before `fe.insertCart(ctx, userID, productID, ...)`, whereas frontend rpc.go insertCart maps UserId/Item.ProductId correctly and cartservice CartService.cs consumes request.UserId / request.Item.ProductId correctly -- so the arguments are passed in the wrong order by the caller. Frontend pod sheet is Running/Ready/0 restarts with no probe, image-pull or mount failures; the mass Warning FailedCreate 'serviceaccount not found' rows are stale setup history because all those ServiceAccounts exist in the live listing (rules out missing_service_account).
